content: This plan aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the region's priorities for preventing and controlling noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) while achieving universal health coverage (UHC). Globally, 2 billion people suffer from vision impairment or blindness, with at least 1 billion cases being preventable or unaddressed. Approximately 90% of those affected live in lowand middle-income countries, and nearly 30% of the world's blind and vision-impaired population resides in the WHO South-East Asia Region. Vulnerable groups, including women, rural populations, and ethnic minorities, are disproportionately affected and face barriers to accessing care. The economic cost of blindness and moderate-to-severe vision loss globally was estimated at $411 billion in 2020. The action plan emphasizes the integration of eye care into primary health care systems and the strengthening of health and social workforces to deliver people-centred services. It sets ambitious targets, including a 40% increase in effective coverage of refractive error correction, a 30% increase in effective cataract surgery coverage, and ensuring that at least 80% of people with diabetes are regularly screened for diabetic retinopathy, with 80% of those identified receiving treatment. Additionally, the plan aims to eliminate trachoma in the region by 2025. The plan outlines five strategic approaches to achieve these goals: 1. Engaging and empowering individuals and communities. 2. Reorienting care models to prioritize primary and community-based services with functional referral systems. 3. Coordinating services across sectors and levels of care. 4. Strengthening and reorienting the eye health workforce. 5. Creating an enabling environment for sustainable eye care delivery. The WHO South-East Asia Regional Office, in collaboration with member states, WHO collaborating centres, and other stakeholders, will provide technical support and monitor progress. The plan also includes a menu of eye care indicators to facilitate tracking and accountability. By implementing these strategies, the region aims to achieve universal eye health and contribute to a healthier, more equitable, and sustainable future.
